samples.summary: 'keeps a concurrent edit to another slide' cannot distinguish a granular splice from a whole-array replacement
samples.evidence: The test captures `untouched = slides()[0]` and `peerEdit = {...untouched.elements[0]}`, then asserts `slides()[0]).toBe(untouched)` and `slides()[0].elements[0]).toEqual(peerEdit)`. The harness root is a plain object (`store.read()`), and `readSlidesRoot` (packages/backend/src/yorkie/slides-tree.ts:52-81) unwraps via `unwrapJson`, which passes plain values through by reference. So even a hypothetical `root.slides = <whole array>` implementation would preserve the identity of `slides()[0]` and the deep-equality of its elements — both assertions hold whether or not the write is granular, which is precisely what the docblock ("only the one slide is written, so nothing else in the array is replaced") claims to prove. `peerEdit` is also a shallow copy of the very object being compared, so `toEqual` is self-satisfying. The real granularity property is genuinely tested one layer down (slide-ops.spec.ts 'carries only the new slide, never a replacement deck' and the moveFront/moveAfterByIndex proxy test), so the behaviour is not uncovered — this controller test just does not add the guarantee it advertises.

samples.summary: New route-collision guard has no positive control: it passes vacuously if handler metadata is ever not found
samples.evidence: The spec's value is entirely in `expect(collisions).toEqual([])`. Every handler is skipped when `Reflect.getMetadata(PATH_METADATA, handler)` is `undefined` (line 63), and nothing asserts that any routes were enumerated at all — `seen` is never inspected. If the metadata key/shape changes (a Nest upgrade, a different `@nestjs/common/constants` import, decorators applied to descriptors rather than the prototype value), every handler is skipped, `collisions` is `[]`, and the spec still reports green while providing zero protection. The only guard present covers controller enumeration (`controllers.length >= 18`, line 42), not handler extraction. The regression it exists to prevent (`POST .../tabs/:tabId/move` shadowing the axis move) is a silently 400-ing published endpoint, so a vacuous guard here lets exactly that class of defect ship again. A `expect(seen.size).toBeGreaterThan(N)` assertion, or a synthetic colliding pair fed through the same normalize/collect logic, would pin it.
searchedFor: grep for PATH_METADATA / METHOD_METADATA usage in backend specs

samples.summary: The backward-move branch of applySlideChange's CRDT path (`moveAfterByIndex(to - 1, from)`) is never exercised
samples.evidence: `applySlideChange`'s 'move' case has three proxy sub-branches: `to === 0` → `moveFront`, `to > from` → `moveAfterByIndex(to, from)`, and otherwise → `moveAfterByIndex(to - 1, from)`. slide-ops.spec.ts's 'reorders in place when the array offers it' (line 170) drives only the first two and asserts `calls` toEqual `['moveFront:ticket-2', 'moveAfterByIndex:2:0']`, so the `to - 1` off-by-one for a backward move to a non-zero position is untested. It is also the only path used in production (a real Yorkie array proxy always has these methods); the plain-array `splice` fallback that the other move tests cover is test-only. Note too that the fake's `moveFront`/`moveAfterByIndex` are no-ops recording call strings, so even the covered branches assert argument values rather than a resulting order — a wrong index would produce a silently mis-ordered deck with no error.

samples.summary: 18 new HttpClient methods are added but their URLs and verbs are never asserted — the CLI test mocks the whole client away
samples.evidence: class-b-commands.test.ts `vi.mock('../src/client/http-client.js')` replaces HttpClient with a stub whose methods only record arguments, so nothing checks that e.g. `moveTab` posts to `/documents/:id/tabs/:tid/reorder` rather than `/move`, or that `deleteComment` targets `/comments/:tid/comments/:cid`. http-client-paths.test.ts (the suite that drives the real client against a stubbed `fetch`) was not extended — it still only covers getDocument/deleteDocument/getCell/getCells/listTabs/getDocContent/revokeApiKey/uploadFileDocument. The `reorder` vs `move` distinction is the entire point of tabs.controller.ts's new docblock, and the path string is duplicated between `http-client.ts#moveTab` and the dry-run preview in `commands/tabs.ts`; a divergence between the two (or a wrong verb) would ship with the suite green, and the dry-run preview would then advertise a URL the client never calls.

samples.summary: Several request-validation guards on the new comments routes have no test
samples.evidence: comments.controller.spec.ts covers empty bodies and PDF anchor validation, but greps for 'must be a boolean', 'JSON object', 'Tab not found' and requireString/asObject in the spec return no matches. Untested guards: `setResolved`'s `'resolved' must be a boolean` (a PATCH with a missing/`"true"`-string field), `asObject`'s non-object/array body rejection on POST and PATCH, `requireString` for a sheet `createThread` missing `tabId` or `ref`, and the `NotFoundException('Tab not found')` when a sheet thread is created against a tab id that does not exist (comments.controller.ts:326). These are the input guards of a public, API-key-reachable write surface; a regression turns a 400 into an unhandled 500 or a thread written with an undefined anchor field. Failures would be loud, which is why this is contained rather than severe.
searchedFor: grep 'must be a boolean|JSON object|Tab not found|requireString|asObject' in packages/backend/src/api/v1/comments.controller.spec.ts

samples.summary: duplicateTab's conditional copying of kind/datasourceId/query metadata is untested
samples.evidence: tab-ops.spec.ts's `duplicateTab` block covers only the name uniquing, insertion position, cell copy and comment dropping. The three conditional metadata carries (`meta.kind`, `meta.datasourceId`, `meta.query`) are never asserted — a fixture whose source tab has those fields is not built in either tab-ops.spec.ts or tabs.controller.spec.ts. Low impact: the controller refuses to duplicate a tab with no worksheet, so the datasource case is largely unreachable today.

finding.summary: New route-collision guard has no positive control: it passes vacuously if handler metadata is ever not found

verdict.reason: The finding's factual observation is accurate — route-collision.spec.ts has no assertion that any handler was enumerated (`seen` is never inspected) — but it does not meet this lens's blocking bar. The spec is not vacuous: it reads the same `controllers` metadata Nest consumes (route-collision.spec.ts:29 vs api-v1.module.ts:54-73), and that enumeration IS pinned by `expect(controllers.length).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(18)` (line 42), which matches the module's exactly-18 controller list. Handler paths come from `PATH_METADATA`, which Nest 11 (package.json:33) defines on the prototype method the spec reads. Crucially, `expect(collisions).toEqual([])` is falsifiable by the precise regression it guards: restoring `@Post(':tabId/move')` on ApiV1TabsController (prefix .../documents/:documentId/tabs) normalizes to the identical key as worksheet-structure.controller.ts:253 `@Post('move')` under prefix .../tabs/:tabId (worksheet-structure.controller.ts:63), and the spec would fail. So it is not an assertion that holds regardless of the behavior, nothing under test is mocked away, and the changed behavior has its own direct coverage (tabs.controller.ts:207 `@Post(':tabId/reorder')` tested at tabs.controller.spec.ts:256-289; the un-shadowed axis move at worksheet-structure-axis.controller.spec.ts:137-151). I searched repo-wide for PATH_METADATA/METHOD_METADATA, other ApiV1Module consumers, router-level e2e enumeration and any seen.size-style assertion, and confirmed no positive-control assertion exists anywhere — so I do not claim a counterexample. What remains is defense-in-depth against a hypothetical future Nest metadata-shape change, which would also break the specs that boot a real Nest app and route over supertest (images.controller.spec.ts:35, documents.controller.spec.ts:442, throttler.spec.ts:54). That is a nit-level hardening suggestion, not fake coverage or a missing test for a changed behavior.
